policy_name: Amadeus AI Policy (Amadeus Group Corporate Policy)
issuing_authority: Amadeus IT Group SA (Corporate and Legal Affairs)
country_region: Global (Amadeus Group, Spain-headquartered; applies beyond the EU)
regulatory_regime: Corporate AI governance aligned with the EU AI Act (self-regulation)
geo_constraints: Applies throughout the Amadeus Group worldwide, not only to operations in the EU

locale_context.regulation: Self-regulation · mandatory group-wide corporate policy built on the EU AI Act
locale_context.culture: European travel-tech multinational that extends EU AI Act categories (prohibited, high-risk, transparency) group-wide as a compliance-first internal rulebook, combined with a GenAI acceptable-use policy and a central use-case review board.

versions.title: Amadeus AI Policy, 10 December 2024
versions.summary: Only one version recorded for this policy.

covered_entities: employees and contractors of Amadeus IT Group SA and its affiliated companies
insofar as possible, non-fully owned companies and distributors
covered_systems: AI tools (AI systems and AI models), incl. ML, logic-based, LLM and generative AI, recommender, chatbots, agents, recognition and analytics systems
GenAI Solutions and GenAI Technology on company or personal devices used for work
covered_activities: procurement, deployment and use of AI tools
conditions: Annex 1 high-risk use cases require prior Legal approval; prohibited practices barred in all cases
use of unapproved GenAI tools tolerated only with [PUBLIC] data
objective: Set a group-wide framework for ethical and lawful development, deployment and use of AI at Amadeus, aligned with the EU AI Act, including a Generative AI Acceptable Use Policy and a list of prohibited and high-risk use cases.

related_policies.policy: EU AI Pact (voluntary pledges; Amadeus is a signatory)

conflict_rule: Applies in addition to other Amadeus policies on the same subjects (AI security standard, security and privacy policies); approval by the AI Use Case Review Board does not exempt other processes.

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/amadeus.pdf). The document carries only the date 10 December 2024 and no version number or change history; effective date assumed to be that date. Not checked whether a newer version exists. binding=false (not law), but the policy is mandatory for employees and contractors: non-compliance can lead to disciplinary action up to termination, and contractor violations may be treated as breach of contract. Referenced annexes/intranet documents (GenAI Acceptable Use Framework, AI Security Standard) are not included in the copy.

clauses.original_text: Do not input sensitive information or personal data into non-approved Gen AI Tools.
clauses.requirement: never put non-public information or personal data into non-approved GenAI tools
clauses.purpose: avoid exposing company, customer and employee data to third parties via model training/outputs
clauses.affected_asset: confidential information; personal data of customers and employees
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI Tools (GenAI Solutions and GenAI Technology), approved or publicly available
clauses.interpretation_notes: Sensitive information = anything not classified [PUBLIC] under the Information Classification and Asset Management Policy, incl. personal data and third-party proprietary information. Use of unapproved tools is tolerated only with [PUBLIC] data.

clauses.original_text: The following practices are strictly prohibited (under the EU AI Act and can result in fines of up to 7% of the total worldwide annual turnover of Amadeus. No one within Amadeus may therefore engage in these practices under any circumstances, including through AI Tools which have been approved: a. Subliminal, manipulative and/or deceptive techniques with the risk of significant harm. … c. Biometric categorization to infer sensitive personal traits. … d. Classification or scoring of people based on behavior or personality characteristics leading to detrimental treatment. … h. Inferring emotions in workplaces and education.
clauses.object: EU AI Act prohibited AI practices (items a–h)
clauses.requirement: no development or deployment of manipulative, exploitative, biometric-categorisation, social-scoring, real-time RBI, predictive-policing, face-scraping or workplace emotion-recognition AI
clauses.purpose: comply with EU AI Act Art. 5 and protect fundamental rights
clauses.affected_asset: natural persons' fundamental rights and autonomy
clauses.applicable_systems: any AI tool, including approved ones
clauses.interpretation_notes: Annex 1 restates the EU AI Act Article 5 prohibitions with travel/industry examples; applied Group-wide, not only in the EU. Items b, e, f and g and the per-item examples elided. The source has an unclosed parenthesis after 'prohibited', kept as printed.

clauses.section: III. General rules for deployment/use of all AI tools
clauses.original_text: All uses of AI tools procured/ deployed by Amadeus need to be registered in the Amadeus AI Inventory. Employees shall log their use case for review and approval of the AI Use Case Review Board: LOP - AI Use Case Intake - Power Apps. This step is mandatory.
clauses.requirement: register every AI use case in the AI Inventory and obtain AI Use Case Review Board approval
clauses.purpose: risk-categorise use cases and route them to the right review
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools (AI systems and models) developed, procured or deployed by the Amadeus Group
clauses.interpretation_notes: Mandatory gate; separately, use cases on the Annex 1 high-risk list need prior Legal approval and prohibited ones may not be procured at all. Board approval does not exempt other processes (IT, CISO, Privacy).

clauses.section: III. General rules for deployment/use of all AI tools
clauses.original_text: We should therefore assign human oversight for the deployment of AI tools to persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support to carry out this oversight well. Generally, everyone who operates the tool should be able to understand how it should work in order to be able to notice when outputs are unreliable and avoid over-reliance on the outputs.
clauses.requirement: competent, trained and authorised humans oversee AI deployments; operators understand the tool to avoid over-reliance
clauses.purpose: catch blind spots, biases and unreliable outputs
clauses.affected_asset: persons affected by AI outputs; Amadeus
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools (AI systems and models) developed, procured or deployed by the Amadeus Group
clauses.interpretation_notes: Mirrors EU AI Act deployer duties (Art. 26). Framed as 'should' within a mandatory policy.

clauses.original_text: Do clearly attribute any output used for business purposes to the GenAI application that created it through a footnote or other means visible to the reader. … all GenAI generated content must be disclosed, cited and reviewed if used for business purposes (e.g. any purpose related to your work at Amadeus) to enable end-users to determine how to consume the content in an informed manner.
clauses.object: GenAI-generated content used for business purposes
clauses.requirement: visibly attribute GenAI output to the tool that produced it and review it before business use
clauses.purpose: transparency to readers and protection against IP claims
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI Tools (GenAI Solutions and GenAI Technology), approved or publicly available
clauses.interpretation_notes: Same section also requires keeping an updated record of GenAI use for business purposes.

clauses.section: IV.2.3 Be critical of outputs and carefully use them
clauses.original_text: Do not use any output that contains material that you suspect to be under copyright protection in any materials, internal or externally facing. … Do not use GenAI Tools to create text, audio, or visual content for purposes of committing fraud or to misrepresent an individual’s identity.
clauses.object: GenAI output suspected to be copyrighted; content for fraud or identity misrepresentation
clauses.requirement: no use of suspected-copyright output; no GenAI content for fraud or impersonation
clauses.purpose: avoid IP infringement and fraudulent or deceptive use
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI Tools (GenAI Solutions and GenAI Technology), approved or publicly available
clauses.interpretation_notes: Two bullets from the same list; the elided bullet forbids relying on information suspected to be inaccurate, inappropriate or biased.
